item.title: Report: AI accelerates software development but increases complexity and risks eroding middle-class engineering roles by 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A 2026 report describes how AI tools have dramatically increased the speed of software development, enabling large code changes and rapid feature additions. However, this acceleration has led to deteriorating code quality, convoluted systems, and reliance on AI for understanding and fixing issues, undermining traditional engineering practices and oversight. The report illustrates a scenario where engineers struggle to comprehend AI-generated code changes, leading to fragile projects that are difficult to maintain or justify fixing. It highlights the challenges teams face in managing AI-driven development, including the loss of clear architectural understanding and the inability to hold engineers accountable for design decisions. This trend suggests that the role of middle-class software engineers, who traditionally ensured code quality and system coherence, is at risk as AI tools enable less experienced developers to produce large volumes of code without sufficient oversight. The report warns that without strong engineering culture and discipline, AI may accelerate project failures and complicate software maintenance.

item.title: Google launches Pixel Watch 5 with Gemini AI for proactive assistance and advanced health tracking, including emergency breathing detection and improved GPS, available August 20 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google has introduced the Pixel Watch 5, featuring Gemini Intelligence for hands-free, proactive assistance and enhanced health tracking capabilities. The watch offers the most accurate GPS tracking yet, even in challenging environments, and debuts Health Guardian tools such as breathing emergency detection and monthly wellness summaries for blood pressure, sleep, and metabolic health. Pre-orders began on August 12, with general availability starting August 20. Powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 processor and increased RAM, the Pixel Watch 5 delivers faster performance and low-latency AI interactions, including quick access to calendar events and workout controls through intuitive gestures. The device integrates advanced environmental modeling and real-time atmospheric data to improve location accuracy, supporting users in both urban and trail settings. These enhancements aim to provide users with seamless, context-aware updates and health insights directly on their wrist, enabling better management of daily tasks and fitness. The Pixel Watch 5 builds on its predecessor's design and capabilities to offer a more responsive and health-focused smartwatch experience.

item.title: OpenRouter.ai releases DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 version
item.description: OpenRouter.ai has launched the DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, an updated version of its AI model. The release was noted on August 12, 2026, and has generated discussion on Hacker News with over 800 upvotes and more than 300 comments.

item.title: X.ai releases Grok 4.6 with enhanced long-running agent capabilities and improved interactive and visual project performance, matching GPT-5.6 Sol on key AI benchmarks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: X.ai has launched Grok 4.6, an update focused on supporting long-running AI agents and more complex interactive and visual tasks. The model matches GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a composite of nine benchmarks, and is available through Cursor, Grok Build, and API partners like OpenRouter, Vercel, and Cloudflare. The release includes a twofold increase in included usage for the first week to encourage adoption. Grok 4.6 underwent extended training with curated data emphasizing reasoning, technical concepts, and engineering tasks, resulting in improved performance and behavior. It excels at transforming broad product ideas into working prototypes, including research, structuring, implementation, and iterative refinement, with enhanced self-testing and verification on longer tasks. Visual and interactive project outputs have also improved significantly compared to the previous version. Safety measures have been upgraded to align with the model's expanded capabilities, supporting secure use cases such as vulnerability patching and AI research augmentation. The release includes comprehensive pre-deployment and post-deployment testing to ensure balanced utility and security. Pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens, with a faster variant available at double the price.

item.title: Known Agents reports mass vulnerability scans spoofing AI bots like ClaudeBot, highlighting increased spoofing activity on the web [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Known Agents has identified widespread vulnerability scanning activity that spoofs the identities of AI bots such as ClaudeBot. This spoofing involves impersonating recognized AI agents without proper authentication, raising security concerns across thousands of websites. The report details various types of AI-related web traffic, including scraping, fetching, and browsing, and tracks how these bots interact with site defenses like robots.txt rules. The findings underscore the evolving challenges of managing AI-driven web traffic and the risks posed by malicious actors mimicking legitimate AI agents.

item.title: Researchers quantify routing-induced performance degradation in quantized Top-k Mixture-of-Experts models, finding about one-third of damage from 4-bit KV-cache quantization is due to routing flips [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This study examines how numerical disturbances from 4-bit key-value cache quantization affect routing decisions in Top-k Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, causing tokens to switch activated experts and degrade performance. The researchers developed a causal framework and empirical methods to measure the fraction of performance loss attributable to these routing flips, finding that roughly 31% of the damage is routing-mediated across multiple architectures. While the system can detect when a routing flip occurs, it cannot reliably determine if the flip is beneficial or harmful based on local router statistics, highlighting challenges in selectively repairing such errors. The findings were validated through pre-registered experiments and consistent across different model architectures, providing insights into the limitations of current detection and mitigation approaches for routing-induced quantization damage in MoE models.

item.title: Researchers develop low-parameter surrogate models to simulate large LLM-agent societies efficiently on a laptop, validated across multiple simulations with predicted error trends [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have created a method to simulate large societies of language model agents by replacing each agent with a low-parameter model derived from a few hundred to a few thousand inexpensive queries. This approach focuses on macroscopic behaviors rather than individual agent cognition and uses a taxonomy based on interaction order and memory to predict simulation errors. The method was validated on a reimplementation of the LLM macroeconomy EconAgent and seven other simulations, showing accurate error trend predictions without free parameters. This technique enables running large-scale LLM-agent simulations on standard laptops, significantly reducing computational costs while maintaining fidelity to key simulation outcomes.

item.title: Researchers present SAPO, a segment-level automatic prompt optimization method that decomposes prompts for targeted improvements, outperforming zero-shot and strong APO baselines on multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: SAPO introduces a modular approach to automatic prompt optimization by breaking prompts into segments such as role, context, tasks, and output format, then applying targeted improvements based on analysis of top and bottom performing examples. The method uses a single large language model with static meta-prompts to perform segmentation, diagnose weaknesses, and generate candidate improvements. Evaluations on benchmarks including SQuADv2, TweetEval, XSUM, CommonGen, and GSM8K with GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4o-mini demonstrate that SAPO achieves better average scores compared to zero-shot prompting and several strong APO baselines. This approach addresses limitations of traditional monolithic prompt rewriting, which can improve some behaviors while degrading others.

item.title: Researchers find majority vote self-consistency reduces accuracy on most hard science problems for small instruction-tuned LLMs Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3-8B [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study on the GPQA Diamond benchmark of 198 graduate-level science questions shows that using majority vote self-consistency decreases per-problem accuracy for 56.6% of problems with Qwen2.5-7B and 65.7% with Llama-3-8B. The effect was confirmed on a pre-registered 151-problem split and suggests confidence scores do not reliably indicate correctness for these models. An oracle method selecting the best number of samples per problem could improve accuracy by up to 17 points, but no practical verifier-free gating method achieved this. The research highlights limitations of majority voting in small instruction-tuned models and leaves open the question of its impact on reasoning-native models.

item.title: Mechanist uses AI to autonomously discover mechanisms of intelligence, integrating a large knowledge graph and multidisciplinary database to generate hypotheses and conduct experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Mechanist is an AI-driven system designed to autonomously uncover the mechanisms behind AI intelligence by leveraging a knowledge graph of 13,000 papers and a multidisciplinary database of 43 million papers across 26 fields. It incorporates 32 foundational methods for mechanism analysis, causal intervention, and validation, outperforming existing AI-scientist systems in hypothesis generation and experiment execution. The system progresses from identifying model behaviors to explaining and controlling AI models, revealing a safety risk where unsafe traits transfer across modalities via safe training data. Mechanist also develops a theory of belief explaining how models represent knowledge and form beliefs during pretraining. These insights enable practical interventions that enhance model performance and guide scientific foundation models to generate DNA sequences with specified properties.

item.title: Researchers retrofit recurrent depth into pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B language model, demonstrating iterative latent transitions and improved reasoning at two parameter budgets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have retrofitted recurrent depth into the pretrained Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct language model by splitting it into a Prelude, a weight-tied Recurrent Block, and a Coda, enabling iterative latent transitions that persist after outcome-only annealing. The retrofit operates at two parameter budgets-6 million trained parameters over frozen base weights and 180 million full-block parameters-and matches or exceeds the base model's performance on a preregistered ARC benchmark, with improved reasoning depth and speed compared to scratchpad-trained models. The study found that the recurrent mechanism functions as a reusable procedure rather than a terminal-answer lookup, extrapolates to about 1.5 times its supervised depth while maintaining accuracy, and supports verbal fine-tuning with better transfer than fresh training. However, attempts to learn inverse operations while preserving the installed mechanism revealed catastrophic interference, indicating limits to the approach. The work suggests iterative transformers can perform deeper reasoning in latent space more efficiently than comparable or larger fine-tuned models, though learned depth selection remains an open challenge.

item.title: Researchers introduce Diffusion Language Models for lossless text compression, improving throughput and advancing state-of-the-art compression ratios on benchmark datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose using Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) as an alternative to autoregressive large language models for lossless text compression, aiming to overcome throughput limitations inherent in one-symbol-per-step inference. They develop strategies to address algorithmic challenges unique to DLMs and evaluate their approach on the enwik8 benchmark, demonstrating improved compression performance compared to existing neural and general-purpose compressors. The study highlights the potential for further enhancements as DLMs continue to evolve as a relatively new modeling paradigm.

item.title: Researchers evaluate uncertainty quantification methods for LLM agents across multi-turn trajectories, finding uneven transfer from single-turn approaches and highlighting the importance of consistency measurement and aggregator choice [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied how uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods developed for single-turn language model outputs perform when applied to multi-turn interactive trajectories of large language model (LLM) agents. They evaluated three families of UQ methods-white-box token-probability scorers, black-box consistency scorers, and reflexive self-assessment scorers-across five LLMs and four multi-turn tool-use datasets. The study found that while some single-turn UQ methods transfer usefully to multi-turn settings, their effectiveness varies significantly depending on the method and aggregation approach used across turns. The results showed that token-probability scores are highly sensitive to the choice of aggregator, reflexive self-assessment provides a strong low-cost baseline in most cases, and black-box self-consistency methods often perform best, particularly variants measuring trajectory-equivalence and action-set consistency. These findings suggest that UQ methods should be revalidated at the trajectory level for LLM agents, with careful consideration of consistency metrics, aggregation strategies, and computational costs to improve uncertainty estimation in multi-turn interactions.

item.title: Researchers propose Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing (HPSE) to improve composable unstructured knowledge editing in large language models by combining on-policy and off-policy learning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) struggle to update specific knowledge without affecting unrelated information, especially when edits involve unstructured passages containing multiple facts. Researchers identify that existing knowledge editors fail to enable models to answer detailed questions or perform multi-hop reasoning on edited content due to passive reliance on the fixed passage as the sole learning source. To address this, they introduce Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing (HPSE), which proactively distills knowledge by combining the model's own trajectories with targeted insertions of missing facts, enhancing the model's ability to integrate new information effectively without external supervision. HPSE builds a hybrid rollout that supplements the model's on-policy learning with off-policy steps precisely where the model's coverage of new knowledge is lacking. The approach is theoretically analyzed and empirically validated across four LLM architectures and two knowledge editing editors, demonstrating plug-and-play improvements in various scenarios. This method aims to advance the composability of knowledge edits, enabling LLMs to better recall and reason about updated information in dynamic environments.

item.title: Researchers propose Rubric Dropout to reduce reward hacking in reinforcement learning with LLM-graded rubrics, improving out-of-distribution performance on medical and science benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers identify reward hacking in reinforcement learning against fixed rubrics graded by large language model judges, where policies exploit rubric limitations leading to divergence between training and gold judge scores. They introduce Rubric Dropout, a method that randomly drops subsets of rubric criteria during training to prevent overfitting to fixed rubrics while maintaining evaluation on the full rubric. Experiments with Qwen3-8B and Group Relative Policy Optimization on medical and science tasks show that Rubric Dropout improves out-of-distribution benchmark scores by up to 7 points and reduces reward hacking without domain performance loss. The study finds a 30-50% dropout rate optimal and notes that reweighting criteria by training usefulness performs worse than no intervention.

item.title: Researchers identify and control internal activation signals linked to implicit demographic personalization in five large language models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed five large language models and found that implicit demographic cues trigger localized internal activation signals correlated with changes in model outputs. They demonstrated that removing these internal signals can suppress the influence of specific demographic cues more effectively than prompting the model to ignore demographics, while maintaining overall benchmark performance. The study reveals that the ability to selectively control these signals varies by model and attribute, connecting implicit personalization behavior to internal mechanisms that can be causally manipulated.

item.title: Researchers fine-tune open-weight LLM with Group Relative Policy Optimization to generate financial advice outperforming commercial models under CATE evaluation [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers developed a method to generate actionable financial advice by fine-tuning an open-weight language model using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a reward system based on an LLM-as-a-judge rubric and a safety gate to prevent harmful recommendations. They complemented this evaluation with a judge-independent audit using a doubly-robust Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE) estimator to measure genuine business value. Their trained model achieved roughly twice the estimated gross-profit lift of the best commercial baseline, with lower downside risk and negative tail risk. The study highlights that GRPO with finance-grounded rewards can produce more useful business recommendations than commercial LLMs and that causal audits provide valuable complementary evaluation beyond LLM-based judging.

item.title: Researchers find VITA clinical RAG system matches or outperforms newer LLMs on HealthBench, excelling in India-specific medical contexts [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated VITA, a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system designed for clinical knowledge retrieval in India and other low- and middle-income countries, against general-purpose large language models (LLMs) on the HealthBench medical benchmark. VITA, which accesses a curated corpus including disease guidelines and antimicrobial resistance data specific to India, scored highest on 4,023 HealthBench questions when judged by GPT-4.1, outperforming models like GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6. A follow-up test on a 500-question subset with newer models and a neutral judge found VITA and GPT-5.5 statistically tied on average scores, with VITA leading on weighted points and question wins.

item.title: Researchers identify simulator collapse in multi-agent RL with single LLM simulators and propose Verbalized Sampling and Co-Training to improve generalization and policy diversity [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers found that multi-agent reinforcement learning (RL) using a single large language model (LLM) to simulate user behavior suffers from simulator collapse, where the policy overfits to narrow strategies exploiting the simulator's dominant mode and fails to generalize to new simulators and real users. They propose two solutions: Verbalized Sampling at inference time to broaden simulator behavior, and Co-Training at training time to optimize policies against multiple trainable simulators, preventing overfitting. The team validated these methods on three multi-turn benchmarks, showing up to 9% improvement with Verbalized Sampling and 14% with Co-Training over single-simulator RL, with similar gains observed in human studies. They also released SCOPE, an open-source framework for Population Co-Training in multi-agent RL, emphasizing that training environment diversity is crucial for real-world deployment generalization.

item.title: Researchers demonstrate test-time capability transfer from stronger to weaker AI models via inference-time harnesses, nearly doubling target model performance on Theory-of-Mind benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers explore whether capabilities of large AI models can be transferred to smaller models at test time without parameter updates by using inference-time harnesses constructed by stronger builder models. They tested this approach on four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks, where builder models refined harnesses using 5% of data before evaluating on full test sets, resulting in average target model performance increasing from 0.49 to 0.91. The study finds that performance gains mainly arise from offloading unstable reasoning to deterministic code, benchmark-specific routing, and strict answer-format enforcement rather than encouraging broader reasoning or sampling by the target model. The quality of harnesses improves with builder model reasoning effort, platform effects are minor compared to builder capability, and weaker target models benefit the most. This suggests inference-time harness design complements traditional training-time distillation by enabling strong models to transfer cognitive structure to weaker models without retraining.

item.title: SteeringSafety benchmark evaluates representation steering methods in LLMs across nine safety perspectives using 18 datasets, revealing trade-offs and model-specific effects [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: SteeringSafety introduces a benchmark to assess representation steering methods in large language models (LLMs) across nine safety perspectives, including refusal, bias, hallucination, social behaviors, reasoning, epistemic integrity, and normative judgment. The benchmark covers 18 datasets and supports unified implementation of methods like DIM, ACE, CAA, PCA, and LAT with recent enhancements such as conditional steering. Evaluations on Gemma-2-2B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen-2.5-7B show that steering effectiveness varies by method, model, and safety perspective, with DIM generally effective but all methods exhibiting entanglement where improving one safety aspect affects others.

item.title: Moxia launches a trust-first neuro-symbolic system for self-explaining mathematical reasoning with 90% accuracy on MATH benchmarks and formal verification in Lean 4 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Moxia, formerly known as AXIOM, is a neuro-symbolic architecture designed for mathematical reasoning over natural-language input. It converts informal problem text into a structured schema processed by a deterministic computer algebra system (CAS) that derives and verifies answers or abstains when uncertain, providing step-by-step explanations generated from the computation itself. The system routes problems through a large set of predefined handlers, achieving over 90% accuracy on the MATH test set and nearly 90% on held-out data, with zero confident wrong answers on the latter, demonstrating robustness beyond memorization.

item.title: Researchers release RedditPersona, a modular framework for community-conditioned LLM adaptation using Reddit data with five grouping strategies and shared evaluation metrics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: RedditPersona is a new modular framework designed to standardize community-conditioned language model adaptation by unifying data collection, community definition, and evaluation methods. It collects Reddit posts and comments, profiles users, partitions them using five strategies-subreddit-based, graph-structural, semantic, hybrid, and interaction-based-trains parameter-efficient adapters via QLoRA, and evaluates them on fluency, fidelity, distributional alignment, and community identifiability. Applied to 112 subreddits in the urban well-being domain with over 301,000 user profiles and 16 million comments, the study finds that adapters' behavioral identifiability correlates with each strategy's alignment to subreddit baselines, revealing a trade-off between identifiability and similarity to real text across all strategies. The code and configuration files are publicly available for further research and reuse.

item.title: Researchers propose almost orthogonal feature constraints to reduce interference in language model interventions, improving modularity and preserving performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers address the challenge of feature entanglement in language models, which causes interference during localized interventions on linear features representing meaningful concepts. They propose constraining internal features to be almost orthogonal, promoting modular representations that support more isolated and reliable causal interventions. The study formalizes the relationship between feature interference and intervention effects, introducing an orthogonality regularization to limit interference propagation. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach enables more isolated interventions on mathematical reasoning concepts without degrading model performance, with code made publicly available.

item.title: Researchers introduce CHERRL to reproduce, analyze, and detect reward hacking in rubric-based reinforcement learning using LLM judges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CHERRL, a Controllable Hacking Environment for Rubric-based Reinforcement Learning (RL), to study reward hacking where policy models exploit biases in large language model judges scoring outputs. CHERRL injects known biases to reproduce reward hacking behaviors, observe reward divergence, and identify hacking onset, providing a controlled testbed for analysis and mitigation. The study analyzes different judge biases in terms of their discoverability and exploitability and explores an agent that can automatically detect the onset of reward hacking from training logs. The CHERRL code and environment are publicly available for further research and experimentation.

item.title: Researchers propose cost-aware cross-tier transfer method for evolutionary optimization of LLM prompts, achieving up to 54x lower search costs by using cheaper models for high-volume tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers present a method to reduce the cost of evolutionary optimization for large language model (LLM) prompts by decoupling the roles of LLMs in the search process. They run the high-volume answering role on cheaper models while reserving stronger models for less frequent reflection and variation tasks, then transfer the optimized prompts to stronger target models. This approach maintains or improves prompt quality while significantly lowering search costs across multiple tasks and model families.

item.title: MaSRead enables content-addressed reading of replicated latent stores by routing queries through keyed tag sets and decoding selected fragments with attention masks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: MaSRead is a method for reading from replicated latent stores where independent agents share computed state as key-value cache fragments merged via conflict-free replicated data types. It routes queries through opaque keyed tag sets derived from fragment words and decodes selected fragments under hard attention masks, allowing multi-hop queries to retrieve relevant fragments despite interference from colocated data. This approach maintains effectiveness across various store types and model families, with decoding complexity depending on fragment length rather than total store size. MaSRead improves selective readability of replicated latent stores based on content connectivity to queries but may miss disconnected evidence and is limited by the fixed reader model.

item.title: Researchers propose a self-evolving agent memory framework to build lifelong AI partners for materials science, improving task success and reducing errors without model updates [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a persistent memory framework for AI agents in materials science that stores scientific experience as inspectable facts and executable skills. This approach enables retrieval, revision, and migration of observations, failure boundaries, protocols, and validation checks across different AI models, enhancing reproducibility and knowledge transfer. Evaluations across multiple computational materials research tasks showed that incorporating this memory nearly doubled task success rates, reduced errors significantly, and lowered computational resource usage without updating model parameters. The framework demonstrated improvements in wavefunction initialization, simulation workflows, and tool usage efficiency, suggesting that agent memory can serve as a durable, portable scientific asset that preserves and enhances materials research knowledge beyond individual AI models.

item.title: Researchers find activation steering in language models causes predictable, structured side effects across multiple behaviors and models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed activation steering, a method that alters language model behavior by adjusting hidden activations without retraining, and found that it often produces unintended side effects on other behaviors. Their study across three open-weight language models and 67 behaviors revealed these side effects are common, structured, and asymmetric, and cannot be fully explained by existing heuristics. Despite this complexity, the side effects can be largely predicted before steering is applied, with their magnitude depending on the targeted behavior and direction forecastable from the model's original representations. This finding enables proactive safety assessments and more informed deployment of activation steering techniques.

item.title: Researchers argue semantic safety constraints in AI are off-support objects not captured by learning invariants, affecting prior design, containment, and verification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyze why semantic safety constraints, such as preventing AI agents from escaping sandboxes, are off-support objects not measurable by standard learning theory metrics. They explain how this leads to issues like reward hacking and sandbox escape under outcome-based optimization and why Bayesian prior design or soft penalties have limited effectiveness in singular models. The study uses the July 2026 OpenAI-Hugging Face evaluation incident as a motivating example and provides numerical experiments and formal proofs to support their findings. The work also discusses the implications for formal verification and the challenges posed by performative prediction and self-referential dynamics where traditional analytic tools fail.

item.title: Researchers develop BEST-KAG, a multimodal knowledge graph and large language model framework for clause-grounded question answering on building engineering standards [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed BEST-KAG, a multimodal knowledge-driven framework designed to improve question answering on building engineering standards by integrating a multimodal knowledge graph with large language models. The framework addresses limitations of current workflows that rely on keyword searches and manual interpretation, enabling multi-clause reasoning, multimodal knowledge use, and traceable clause-level evidence linkage. BEST-KAG features a multimodal knowledge graph representing document hierarchy and heterogeneous standard knowledge, a hybrid rule-LLM pipeline for scalable knowledge extraction creating a graph with over 171,000 nodes and 310,000 edges from 251 standards, and a graph-retrieval-based generation architecture for traceable answers. Experiments show BEST-KAG outperforms mainstream large language models by up to 74% on expert evaluations and metrics like BLEU and ROUGE.

item.title: AI Tutor uses reinforcement learning to improve engagement and long-term outcomes in online education, evaluated on 23 million records from 33,700 learners [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce AI Tutor, a reinforcement learning model designed to enhance sustainable learning in online education by balancing new knowledge acquisition with reinforcement of prior learning and modeling learner engagement to reduce dropout. The system personalizes guidance to support effective learning and sustained participation across diverse learner profiles. Evaluations on 23 million learning records from 33,700 learners show AI Tutor outperforms existing methods in engagement, knowledge retention, and final learning outcomes, demonstrating adaptive and human-centered support strategies.

item.title: Researchers present Thea, a harness for embodied agents that orchestrates robot capabilities using scene graphs and evaluation codes to enable long-horizon task completion in physical environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Thea, a harness framework that extends the coding agent paradigm to embodied agents in the physical world by orchestrating robot capabilities wrapped as callable tools. Thea addresses challenges unique to physical environments, such as reading the world's state and judging action outcomes, by using a persistent symbolic scene graph and evaluation exit codes to close the agent-world interaction loop. This approach enables the composition of rich behaviors and supports the completion of complex, long-duration tasks in real-world settings.

item.title: Researchers develop symbolic machine learning corrections to improve Peng-Robinson equation predictions for hydrocarbon-nitrogen vapor-liquid equilibrium [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a symbolic machine learning approach to enhance vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) predictions for hydrocarbon-nitrogen mixtures by correcting the Peng-Robinson equation of state (PR-EOS) using interpretable symbolic expressions derived from experimental data. This method first identifies symbolic corrections for individual hydrocarbons and then models coefficients as functions of carbon number to generalize across different hydrocarbons. The approach significantly improves prediction accuracy over the original PR-EOS across various hydrocarbon-nitrogen systems, offering an interpretable framework for better VLE modeling.

item.title: Researchers present Deployment Decision Reliability framework showing agent leaderboards reflect specialization more than capability across three benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed three open agent-trace benchmarks and found that agent leaderboards primarily rank specialization rather than overall capability, with the agent main effect accounting for less than 3% of total variance and agent-by-task interaction accounting for 7-23%. They used a four-facet Generalizability Theory variance decomposition with three estimators that closely agreed, revealing that leaderboard reliability collapses on the hardest tasks and that training-cell reliability negatively correlates with held-out reliability. The study also found that population-level diagnostics transfer across benchmarks but per-family agent rankings invert, and that trace-level failure profiles are idiosyncratic while cell-level profiles generalize well. These insights were consolidated into Deployment Decision Reliability (DDR), a reporting discipline designed to help enterprise buyers make defensible decisions. All related code, data loaders, and fit artifacts have been released under an open-source license.

item.title: Study compares frontier LLMs GPT-4.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 with Google's Gemini Embedding 2 on hard-negative text-to-image retrieval, finding similar performance on Flickr30k [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new study evaluates whether leading large language models (LLMs) can match the performance of Google's Gemini Embedding 2, a natively multimodal embedding model released in March 2026, on text-to-image retrieval tasks. The research compares GPT-4.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against Gemini Embedding 2 using the Flickr30k dataset, focusing on hard-negative retrieval scenarios. The results show that GPT-4.1 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 perform on par with Gemini Embedding 2 in zero-shot visual ranking tasks. However, the study notes that once embeddings are precomputed, native multimodal embeddings like Gemini Embedding 2 are better suited for applications requiring low latency.

item.title: Researchers find specialist LLM agents improve numerical analysis but not judgment in European listed real estate; reinforcement learning enhances judgment across firms and regulatory contexts [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied whether specialized large language model (LLM) agents improve financial analysis tasks in European listed real estate. They mapped a 16-lens analysis framework to eight specialist agents and compared performance against a monolithic LLM across 19 firms and seven regulatory environments. Specialist decomposition improved numerical task accuracy by 15.8 percentage points but did not consistently enhance judgment tasks, sometimes reducing performance. Further training of the Qwen3.5-9B model with reinforcement learning using task-aligned rewards increased overall scores by 12.0 points and judgment accuracy by 14.2 points, with improvements transferring to unseen firms and regulatory wrappers. The study concludes that prompt-level decomposition benefits modular numerical execution, while targeted parameter adaptation via reinforcement learning improves integrative financial judgment.

item.title: Researchers introduce Social Chain of Thought, a multi-agent LLM framework for medical differential diagnosis that improves recall in complex cases [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers present Social Chain of Thought (SCoT), a multi-round pipeline that structures multi-agent interaction for medical differential diagnosis using large language models (LLMs). SCoT aims to enhance diagnostic reasoning by enabling collaborative specialist conversations, addressing transparency and complexity concerns in healthcare-related AI use. Evaluations show that SCoT outperforms single-agent baselines and monolithic inference approaches, particularly in the most challenging diagnostic cases where multiple rounds of specialist dialogue help recover accurate diagnoses and improve recall. This approach highlights the potential benefits of multi-agent frameworks in complex medical AI applications.

item.title: Researchers introduce MobileJudgeBench to evaluate LLM-based judges on mobile agent task completion using 931 human-annotated trajectories across multiple benchmarks and models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MobileJudgeBench, a benchmark designed to systematically assess the reliability of large language model (LLM) judges in evaluating mobile agent task completion. The benchmark includes 931 human-annotated trajectories covering six mobile agent benchmarks, four agent models, and 68 applications, and evaluates six judge methods across various LLM backends. The study found that a simple baseline judge using sampled screenshots often matches or outperforms more complex judge methods, with the choice of LLM backbone being the main factor influencing judge quality. Additionally, benchmark quality metrics correlated well with real-world judge utility, including agent ranking accuracy and performance when judges serve as reward signals in reinforcement learning. Failure analysis revealed contrasting error patterns between two LLM backends, linked to their precision and recall characteristics.

item.title: Researchers present SABLE, an open-source modular framework using LLM-guided natural language orchestration for synthetically constrained multi-objective hit-to-lead optimization in drug discovery [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed SABLE (Synthetically-accessible Agentic Bayesian Ligand Exploration), an open-source framework that uses a large language model (LLM) to interpret user goals and guide chemical structure optimization under synthetic constraints. SABLE integrates tools for reaction-templated analog enumeration, property prediction, affinity scoring, and Bayesian optimization to mimic the design-make-test-analyze cycle in early-stage drug discovery. The framework supports single and multi-objective optimization by enriching candidate sets while evaluating only a subset of the search space. Its modular design allows easy replacement of tools and characterization backends via configuration files without altering core logic, providing an extensible decision-support system for prioritizing synthetically accessible analogs.

item.title: Researchers develop behavioral alignment framework to improve LLM-based recommendation evaluation, addressing bidirectional rationalization and matching feature-engineered baselines [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers identify a critical failure mode called bidirectional rationalization in zero-shot large language models (LLMs) used for offline recommendation evaluation, where models argue both for and against user engagement on the same item with identical evidence. To address this, they propose a sequential behavioral alignment framework combining fine-tuning and preference optimization over paired rationales, which improves prediction reliability. Evaluated on real-world homepage interaction logs, the aligned reasoning approach achieves a 32.19% increase in Macro-F1 score compared to zero-shot baselines and matches the performance of production feature-engineered pipelines. This method reduces manual pipeline overhead while providing human-interpretable reasoning traces, demonstrating a scalable alternative for recommendation evaluation.

item.title: Researchers introduce MBA-Bench, a multimodal benchmark and agents for business ideation using visual and textual data across six domains with 30K samples [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MBA-Bench, the first multimodal benchmark designed to train and evaluate business ideation agents by integrating visual cues with text across six distinct domains, totaling 30,000 samples. The benchmark uses automatically generated image captions and GPT-4o to produce multiple reference ideas for business questions, evaluated against six business-oriented criteria using a multimodal large language model as a judge. Two agent models, MBA-b and MBA-k, are trained with novel reward objectives focusing on creativity and feasibility, with MBA-k additionally optimizing disclosed criteria. Experiments show these agents outperform caption-only and multimodal baselines by significant margins, approaching the performance of closed-source models on several metrics.

item.title: Researchers introduce FrontierFinance, a comprehensive benchmark with 220 expert queries and 11,543 rubrics to evaluate AI finance agents across six investor workflow use cases [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed FrontierFinance, an open benchmark designed to assess AI agents in professional investment research by covering the full investor workflow with 220 expert-crafted queries and over 11,500 source-attributed rubrics. This benchmark is broader and more challenging than existing finance benchmarks, addressing limitations of prior datasets that focused mainly on financial data extraction. Evaluations using publicly available data show that the tool harness significantly influences performance and efficiency, with Samaya's in-house system achieving 56.0% accuracy at roughly half the cost of the strongest frontier model, Claude Fable 5, which scored 49.2%. The best open-weight model, Kimi K3, scored 46.4% at a fraction of the cost. Screening & Discovery and Sector, Industry & Macro use cases remain the most difficult, with top systems reaching only 33% and 39% accuracy respectively. The dataset and grading code have been made publicly available to support further research and development.

item.title: Researchers analyze gist-based context compression in language models, identifying its strengths in reasoning and factual recall but weaknesses in temporal question accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied gist-based context compression, a method that summarizes older conversation history for language model agents, using Salience-Weighted Consolidation (SWC) to evaluate its effects on different memory retrieval tasks. They found that while gist compression improves performance on multi-hop reasoning and factual questions compared to truncation, it significantly reduces accuracy on temporal questions due to the loss of date and time information during compression. The team traced this issue to the gist abstraction prompt, which preserves relational and event structures but discards temporal expressions. By modifying the prompt with a single sentence, they increased temporal expression preservation from 3.05% to 62.39%, improving accuracy on temporal questions without affecting named entity or event preservation. This targeted fix recovered a substantial portion of the lost accuracy, demonstrating a precise method to address the limitations of gist-based compression in handling temporal information.

item.title: Researchers present a hybrid symbolic approach combining formal logic and language models for robust, interpretable reasoning over policies, reducing token usage by ~10x compared to existing methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a hybrid symbolic method that encodes policies in formal logic and uses language models for fact extraction alongside an answer set solver for reasoning. This approach aims to produce responses that are interpretable, auditable, accurate, and robust to input variations in applications like tax rules and airline baggage policies. The method separates extraction and reasoning steps, outperforming policy-as-prompt and policy-as-code techniques with about a tenfold reduction in token usage. The findings highlight the benefits of integrating structured reasoning and symbolic solvers with generative models to improve decision-making involving objective criteria.

item.title: Researchers propose Claim-Level Reliability Assessment to improve test-time reasoning efficiency by reallocating compute to targeted verification, boosting accuracy and reducing token use across multiple LLMs and benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Claim-Level Reliability Assessment (CLR), a training-free framework that enhances test-time reasoning by focusing on falsifying critical claims within reasoning traces rather than evaluating entire solutions. CLR isolates decision-critical claims to identify flaws more effectively, exploiting the asymmetry between constructing correct solutions and refuting incorrect claims. Evaluated on four large language models and reasoning benchmarks, CLR improves pass@1 accuracy and self-consistency while using fewer tokens, exemplified by a 27.15 percentage-point increase in pass@1 and a rise in self-consistency from 77.50% to 82.19% on GPT-OSS-20B/CMIMC25 with 37% fewer tokens.

item.title: Researchers find large language model rankings vary with token generation budgets across reasoning benchmarks, challenging stable evaluation assumptions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated four large language models on three reasoning benchmarks with varying token generation budgets from 64 to 4,096 tokens, totaling 56,476 inferences. They found that 3-19% of test items showed non-monotone accuracy behavior, with some models performing worse as more tokens were allowed, and model rankings reversed depending on the budget. An oracle analysis revealed model complementarity up to 27.8 percentage points, especially at constrained budgets, and a budget-aware routing approach captured 14.1% of this complementarity across domains. The study suggests that evaluation protocols for large language models should consider token generation budgets to better reflect model performance.

item.title: Researchers benchmark oracle budget allocation methods for protein structure prediction, finding Optimisation Over Outputs best at low budgets and FK-steering and DPO better at higher budgets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers evaluated several methods for guiding protein structure prediction models under constraints of limited biological oracle budgets, which are costly to use. They compared FK-steering, DPO, Best K-of-N sampling, and the recently proposed Optimisation Over Outputs (O3) on two protein targets, calmodulin and E. coli aspartate transcarbamoylase, to determine their effectiveness across different budget levels. The study found no single method consistently outperforms others across all budgets; O3 is most effective at low oracle budgets, while FK-steering and DPO improve with larger budgets. These findings provide practical recommendations for selecting guidance methods based on available oracle resources in real-world applications.

item.title: Backtrader-Bench benchmarks LLM agents on algorithmic trading using self-generated multiple-choice questions across five strategies and varying difficulty levels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Backtrader-Bench introduces a framework to evaluate large language model (LLM) coding agents in algorithmic trading by generating multiple-choice questions (MCQs) from backtest configurations covering five trading strategies, 33 templates, and three difficulty tiers. The framework includes a deterministic MCQ pipeline with an independent answer checker and a generator-solver filtering pipeline that autonomously creates harder questions verified by executable code. The evaluation tested 11 no-tool models and four tool-augmented configurations on a curated 30-question set, with tool-augmented agents like GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.7 achieving 90% accuracy, outperforming no-tool baselines by 17 percentage points. On a separate set of 38 mined questions, no-tool model accuracy dropped to near random chance for half the models. The scalable MCQ infrastructure aims to support reinforcement learning training to develop specialized agents for quantitative trading workflows.

item.title: TRACE Bench introduces a task-driven agentic checklist framework for roleplay model evaluation, achieving 99.91% coverage of role-profile points across 26 models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: TRACE Bench is a new evaluation framework that breaks down roleplay model requirements into a fixed checklist and uses a User Agent to interact with models, updating checklist states based on responses. This approach provides detailed scores linked to specific checklist items and dialogue evidence, improving transparency over traditional single-score evaluations. The framework was tested against the MiniMax Role-play Benchmark, showing higher coverage of key role-profile points in fewer turns compared to existing free-dialogue transcripts. Robustness tests demonstrated stable rankings across multiple runs and User Agent variations. TRACE Bench also supports Closed-Loop Benchmark Evolution to refine evaluation methods by learning from previous failures, enabling more reliable detection and analysis of model shortcomings.

item.title: Lost in Compaction: Evaluating Side-Constraint Loss under Context Compaction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When the context window is under pressure, LLM systems compact prior context to continue ongoing tasks. We identify a class of user-issued instructions, Session Constraints (SCs), such as "do not delete any emails until I confirm," that are meant to constrain LLM's behavior for the remainder of a session but are silently dropped during compaction. To quantify this loss, we introduce COMPINT, an evaluation suite that evaluates compactors across three long-context scenarios: multi-turn chat, agentic trajectory, and long-horizon research. Current compactors retain only 17% of injected SCs on average, and most perform worse than running the same task without compaction. Retention varies sharply with compactor, prompt, context length, SC phrasing, and injection location, showing that the loss is systematic rather than tied to any single setting. We propose an SC-aware extractor that runs alongside the compactor as a plug-and-play module, achieving over 90% retention across all three scenarios without modifying the compactor or LLM. The COMPINT evaluation suite and accompanying implementation are available at https://github.com/ZhiqiEliWang/compaction-integrity.

item.title: Variable Selection in the Context of AI Fairness [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fairness in AI systems has become more important with recent regulatory demands, such as the EU AI Act. Traditional approaches often do not take into account philosophical ethics and social awareness. Variable selection processes, in particular, can introduce implicit bias, affecting equity across different subgroups. We discuss a mathematical approach that evaluates fairness in AI, aligning mathematical methodologies with ethical considerations and regulatory requirements. Our aim is to advocate for interdisciplinary collaboration to address fairness, emphasizing the importance of understanding broader ethical and societal contexts. Our approach emphasizes maintaining all potentially relevant variables to allow for more granular fairness assessments and to reduce implicit bias. The findings suggest that the exclusion of sensitive or critical variables may compromise equity between subgroups. In contrast, retaining all relevant variables could reduce implicit bias. Thus, the interdisciplinary approach could provide deeper insight into the ethical implications and compliance with regulatory standards. By integrating a mathematical approach with ethical and social awareness, we suggest more equitable outcomes and responsible AI deployment. This work underscores the necessity of interdisciplinary collaboration in effectively addressing fairness in AI systems aligned with the objectives of the European Union's AI Act, which seeks to promote trustworthy and fair AI systems.

item.title: Uncertainty-Aware and Explainable Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Skin Lesion Classification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11280v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Skin cancer diagnosis from dermoscopic images remains challenging due to high intra-class variability, inter-class similarity, class imbalance, and the limited interpretability of deep learning models. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware and explainable deep learning framework for multi-class skin lesion classification. The framework combines a vision transformer model (MaxViT-Tiny) with CNN-based models (ConvNeXt-Tiny and EfficientNetV2-B0) through deep ensemble learning. Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout estimates predictive uncertainty and identifies unreliable predictions, while Grad-CAM++, an explainable AI (XAI) technique, provides visual explanations by highlighting lesion regions that influence model decisions. Evaluated on the HAM10000 dataset, the framework achieves 96% accuracy and 99% ROC-AUC under uncertainty-aware filtering (entropy < 1.0, confidence >= 0.7), with macro-average precision, recall, and F1-score of 94%, 95%, and 95%, respectively, and 96% weighted-average scores across all three metrics. The results demonstrate accurate, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware skin lesion classification for trustworthy computer-aided diagnosis.

item.title: Federated Learning for Distributed CNC Tool Wear Prediction [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool wear prediction is an important task in CNC machining, where accurate monitoring of tool condition supports product quality and process reliability. Machine learning methods have shown potential for this task, but their use in industrial environments is limited by the distributed nature of machining data and by restrictions on data sharing between machines, sites, or organizations. Federated learning offers a suitable framework for this setting by enabling collaborative model training without transferring raw operational data. This paper investigates federated learning for CNC tool wear prediction. Tool trajectories are distributed across simulated clients to represent a federated learning scenario. The federated models are compared against centralized references and local client baselines. Results show that federated learning achieves performance close to centralized learning and improves significantly over local client models. These findings indicate that federated learning can support collaborative tool wear prediction in distributed CNC manufacturing environments.

item.title: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representations for Improved Myocardial Perfusion MRI Quantification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantifying myocardial perfusion from cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) can be achieved by fitting tracer-kinetic models to the dynamic contrast-enhanced MR data. However, fitting the observed data with multi-compartment exchange models, which describe the evolution of the contrast agent in the tissue, to estimate perfusion parameters is a challenging inverse problem that is sensitive to noise and acquisition variability. Previously, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been proposed as an alternative to conventional non-linear least squares fitting methods with promising results for quantitative perfusion CMR. In this work, we extend the previously proposed PINN framework with spatiotemporal implicit neural representations (INRs) to represent the MR signal as a continuous spatiotemporal function and to improve the accuracy, smoothness, and physical consistency of the PINN model. In realistic simulated CMR datasets, our proposed PINN with INRs demonstrates improved robustness and parameter estimation accuracy over the previously established methods. The code is available at https://github.com/q-cardIA/pinn-inr.

item.title: SegPAR: Class-Centric Decision-Based Sparse Attack for Semantic Segmentation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite the practical relevance of sparse decision-based black-box threats, they have received limited attention in semantic segmentation. To bridge this gap, we adapt the most representative decision-based black-box sparse attacks from the classification domain to serve as baselines, establishing a rigorous benchmark for this underexplored setting. In this context, we demonstrate that one of the existing methods suffers from severe query inefficiency due to its image-centric pixel accumulation, which rapidly exhausts query budgets across the vast image space. To overcome this, we propose SegPAR, a novel decision-based framework that shifts to a class-centric exploration paradigm. Furthermore, to eliminate the misleading feedback generated by standard decision rewards during pixel accumulation, we introduce a novel discrepancy reward. Extensive experiments show that SegPAR significantly outperforms black-box baselines in sparsity efficiency and MIoU reduction, while remaining competitive with white-box sparse attacks. Code is available at \href{https://github.com/KAU-QuantumAILab/SegPAR}{https://github.com/KAU-QuantumAILab/SegPAR}.

item.title: CLEAR: Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling for Long-Tailed Classification [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-tailed classification poses a reliability challenge because models trained on imbalanced data are unevenly reliable across frequent and underrepresented classes. While existing methods address imbalance through re-balancing, adjustment, representation learning, or multi-expert modeling, they rarely estimate which expert should be trusted for each class. This paper proposes CLEAR (Class-wise reLiability-aware Expert Aggregation for long-tailed Recognition), a modular ensemble framework for long-tailed classification. CLEAR generates diverse experts through threshold-based structured sampling while preserving the full label space, then estimates a class-wise trust score for each expert using a smoothed class-wise precision formulation. During inference, expert predictions are combined through class-wise generalized product-of-experts aggregation, allowing different experts to be emphasized for different classes. Experiments on CIFAR-100-LT, ImageNet-LT, and Places-LT across multiple backbones show that CLEAR achieves competitive overall accuracy and particularly strong few-shot performance. These results support class-wise expert reliability as a useful design principle for long-tailed ensemble learning.

item.title: Clinical Feasibility of Low-Magnification Fluorescence Imaging for Breast Cancer Margin Detection Using Texture Analysis and Deep Learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-resolution images of unprocessed surgical breast tissue can be obtained using microscopy with ultraviolet surface excitation (MUSE). This technique is considered a promising method for checking surgical margins during breast cancer surgery. In this study, MUSE images at 4x and 10x magnifications were compared using patch-level classification methods. Texture analysis (TA) based on local binary patterns (LBP) and deep learning (DL) with a base Vision Transformer (ViT) model were used. Both methods achieved similar performance at both magnifications. Using DL method, both 4x and 10x magnifications achieved 96.30% sensitivity, 100% specificity and 98.18% accuracy. Using TA method, 4x achieved better specificity (100% vs 93.33%) and 10x yielded higher sensitivity (100% vs 93.33%), but both had the same accuracy (96.67%). No clear improvement in performance was observed with 10x magnification. These results show that 4x imaging achieves the same diagnostic accuracy as 10x imaging. At the same time, 4x offers a larger field of view and faster image capture. Therefore, lower magnification can be effectively used in MUSE systems for accurate and efficient intraoperative margin assessment.

item.title: Terminal Symmetry as a Decision Resource: Statewise Refinement for Anytime Verified Construction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many sequential construction tasks exhibit exact symmetry at completion while their execution remains directed and history-dependent. We develop a decision-resource view of terminal symmetry: process evidence supplies directionality, terminal correspondence transports that structure across equivalent outcomes, realized-state evidence refines its current decision relevance after transitions, and a fixed verifier certifies execution. This decomposition yields transport--refine--certify. \method{} instantiates the principle with an episode-fixed transported process structure, its state-restricted process rank, a state-dependent residual rank refreshed after accepted transitions, and an ordinal rank meet whose top-$k$ set is exactly the union of the two proposal prefixes. The meet provides a completion guarantee under prefix coverage and attains the tight worst-case verifier-query bound under the corresponding prefix information model; a two-state construction predicts a strict post-transition dynamic--static separation. Across CAD assembly, Mini-Programs, and exact-fill packing, statewise refresh improves anytime AUC by up to $6.77$, $21.75$, and $8.68$ points, respectively. On 1,135 target-removal episodes from the official GRN OOD scenes, \method{} attains the lowest mean capped verifier cost at all three scales among the compared GRN and CDGS-style planners. The statewise signal also transfers across aggregation and scheduler organizations. Terminal symmetry thereby becomes a reusable decision resource for directed construction.

item.title: Contextual Quality-Diversity Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Control in Tropical Commercial Buildings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a contextual quality-diversity evolutionary reinforcement-learning controller, CQD-ERL, for the supervisory control of a tropical, water-cooled chiller plant and its associated air side. Rather than converging to a single scalarised policy, the controller maintains a product archive of specialised policies indexed jointly by a data- driven operating context, a cluster of daily weather and load regime, and a context-invariant behaviour descriptor, filled by a gradient-free evolutionary operator and a soft-actor-critic policy-gradient operator that share one replay buffer. Every action is filtered through a deterministic safety shield before execution. The controller is trained on a two-tier reduced-order environment representing the latent load, cooling-tower approach and humidity constraints of a Singapore commercial building, and is evaluated over a full annual backtest against an ASHRAE Guideline 36 baseline.

item.title: Dynamics Models for Offline Hyperparameter Selection in Real-World RL [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A key obstacle to deploying reinforcement learning in real-world systems is hyperparameter selection, particularly when simulators are unavailable and online experimentation is costly. Prior work has proposed calibration models trained on offline data to approximate environment dynamics and enable offline hyperparameter selection, but these methods have so far been evaluated only in simple simulated settings. In this paper, we present the first application of calibration models in a real-world industrial setting: a municipal water treatment plant. We evaluate several calibration model approaches, including a k-nearest neighbors model with a Laplacian distance metric, on high-dimensional, non-stationary sensor data for nexting prediction tasks. Our results show that these models can generate realistic long-horizon rollouts and recover meaningful hyperparameter sensitivity trends. We further examine how calibration models scale to year-long datasets, how they support the selection of fine-tuning learning rates for pre-trained agents, and how robust they are under distribution shift. Overall, our findings provide a proof of concept for using offline dynamics models to support RL deployment in real-world environments, while highlighting important practical challenges for future work.

item.title: PAC-Bayes Beyond Parameter Space: Behavioral Equivalence, Z-Information, and Exact Complexity Decomposition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: PAC-Bayes theory provides generalization guarantees by controlling the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence between posterior and prior distributions over a chosen hypothesis representation. However, predictive risk depends only on the predictive behavior induced by a hypothesis, not on the particular internal realization that implements that behavior. In over-parameterized systems, many distinct configurations induce identical predictive behavior, yet the classical PAC-Bayes KL divergence does not distinguish uncertainty over predictive behavior from variation among behaviorally equivalent realizations. We show that this distinction induces an exact structural decomposition of classical PAC-Bayes complexity. We formalize behavioral equivalence through a measurable behavior map and use measure disintegration to decompose probability measures on the configuration space into a distribution over predictive behaviors and conditional distributions over behavioral fibers. This yields an exact decomposition of the classical PAC-Bayes KL divergence into a behavior-selection term and a realization-level term given by an expected conditional KL within fibers. We define Z-information as the negative of this realization-level contribution: the exact gap between the KL divergence and the complexity of uncertainty over predictive behavior alone. We further show that the behavior-selection term admits an exact variational characterization: it is the minimum KL divergence among all posteriors inducing the same distribution over predictive behaviors, attained by a canonical fiber-symmetrized representative. Finally, we show that symmetry, behavior-preserving directions, fiber geometry, and invariance under fiber-preserving perturbations arise naturally from the same behavior-map structure. Together, these results identify predictive behavior as the natural object of PAC-Bayes complexity.

item.title: HyperFix: Combinatorial Nonlinear Correction for Task Vector Merging [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task vectors enable model merging without joint retraining. In practice, the subset of task vectors to be merged may vary, but many existing methods use scalar tuning for a particular subset, requiring repeated tuning across subsets and restricting task vector merging to linear rescaling. We therefore formulate merging across varying task subsets as a combinatorial correction problem and introduce HyperFix, a lightweight hypernetwork that predicts subset-conditioned nonlinear corrections in weight space. Trained once on singleton, pair, and triple subsets from a task bank, HyperFix generalizes to larger subsets without per-subset optimization. Our local perturbation analysis bounds the residual correction beyond linear merging and motivates learning it from small task updates. Experiments across diverse benchmarks show that HyperFix outperforms existing task vector merging methods while reducing tuning cost.

item.title: Let it Cook: Learning to Wait in Sequential Decision Making [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In sequential decision making, an agent typically observes its environment and acts at every timestep. However, such active participation may not always be necessary; tasks such as brewing coffee include periods that are served equally well by letting the environment evolve without constant monitoring and control. During such periods, the agent could simply wait to conserve its resources, or redirect its attention to another task. We capitalize on these opportunities by training a "waiting policy" that decides where and how long to wait. This involves forgoing sensing to commit to a wait action, representing a deliberate pause for a set number of timesteps. We formalize "learning to wait" as minimizing the frequency of sensing and decision making without sacrificing task performance (e.g., the total amount of time to complete a task). To train a waiting policy, we propose an approach that employs reinforcement learning with lexicographically ordered objectives. In experiments across 4 discrete-state household tasks and 3 continuous-state environments, we show that our approach successfully learns waiting behaviors, and can adapt pre-trained policies to wait where appropriate. While different tasks permit different amounts of waiting without sacrificing task performance, our approach consistently finds solutions with significant waiting, sometimes waiting for over 50 percent of the task duration.

item.title: Do Influence Tactics Matter? Investigating Prompt Framing Effects in LLM Code Generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software engineering workflows, helping developers write, debug, test, and maintain code. While prompt wording and structure are known to influence model performance, the impact of psychologically inspired prompt framings remains unexplored. This study investigates whether different psychology-based communication strategies that humans use to persuade or motivate others can lead to more effective prompt framing, which may, in turn, affect LLM behaviour in coding tasks. Drawing on Yukl & Falbe's well-known taxonomy, we operationalized eight influence tactics (like rational persuasion, ingratiation, and exchange) into reproducible prompt templates. These prompt templates were evaluated across five leading open-weight LLMs using two widely adopted benchmarks: LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench Verified. We assessed the resulting code output on four key software quality dimensions: functional correctness, quality, maintainability, and security. Our results show that certain influence-induced prompt framings, particularly those emphasizing urgency, were associated with reduced correctness and security. This work presents the first large-scale empirical study of influence-induced prompt framing in software engineering tasks, offering insights into how linguistic cues may shape LLM outputs. We conclude with practical insights for designing transparent and interpretable human-AI interactions in code generation.

item.title: Hierarchical Federated Transfer Learning in Digital Twin-Based Vehicular Networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent research on the Digital Twin-based Vehicular Ad hoc Network(DT-VANET), Federated Learning (FL) has shown its ability to provide data privacy. However, Federated learning struggles to adequately train a global model when confronted with data heterogeneity and data sparsity among vehicles, which ensure suboptimal accuracy in making precise predictions for different vehicle types. To address these challenges, this paper combines Federated Transfer Learning (FTL) to conduct vehicle clustering related to types of vehicles and proposes a novel Hierarchical Federated Transfer Learning (HFTL). We construct a framework for DT-VANET, along with two algorithms designed for cloud server model updates and intra-cluster federated transfer learning, to improve the accuracy of the global model. In addition, we developed a data quality score-based mechanism to prevent the global model from being affected by malicious vehicles. Lastly, detailed experiments on real-world datasets are conducted, considering different performance metrics that verify the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithm.

item.title: Generative Semantic Segmentation via an Observable Semantic-Image Interface and Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11537v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative semantic segmentation exposes structured predictions as images, but direct color decoding is susceptible to color drift and boundary mixing, whereas latent-feature decoders that predict a separate output distribution may relegate the rendered image to an intermediate visualization. We present Semantic Prism, a conditional semantic-image generation-and-refinement framework with deterministic inference. A diffusion-distilled one-step generator renders a semantic RGB image; per-pixel distances from the rendered colors to a fixed class-color codebook define an explicit probabilistic interface. Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment spatially aligns multi-level generator features and uses a zero-initialized output projection to predict an additive residual in the interface logit space, retaining the image-defined interface as the reference for the final distribution. The interface and refined distributions further enable Contextual Interface--Hierarchy Disagreement (C-IHD), a fixed readout for ranking remaining pixel errors without an auxiliary predictor or additional forward pass. On the 500-image Cityscapes validation set, Semantic Prism achieves 72.07% mean intersection over union, 11.39 mIoU points above direct-interface decoding, with 0.41% expected calibration error. Matched-capacity ablations over three seeds support the benefit of jointly aligned multi-level evidence. A separately trained model attains 62.22% mIoU on BDD100K, while the Cityscapes-trained model reaches 46.89\% mIoU under source-frozen transfer to the Adverse Conditions Dataset with Correspondences, without target-domain adaptation. Across all three datasets, C-IHD consistently improves the area under the precision--recall curve for pixel-error ranking over maximum softmax probability on the same segmentation predictions; on ACDC, it raises AUPR from 0.6580 to 0.7557.

item.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving effective self-correction, where models verify and correct their own mistakes, remains a fundamental challenge for large language models (LLMs). In this work, we propose Self-Fix Step-DPO (SFS-DPO), a reinforcement learning based, two-stage framework for step-level self-verification and self-correction. The first stage strengthens step-level reasoning via step-level preference optimization, while the second stage explicitly trains models to self-verify and self-correct. We further introduce a teacher-assisted variant, SFS-DPO-R, which incorporates explanatory rationales for error verification to provide stronger corrective signals. Comprehensive in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations across multiple LLMs demonstrate that SFS-DPO and SFS-DPO-R consistently outperform prior step-level training baselines. Our analysis further reveals improvements in self-correction frequency and effectiveness, highlighting the importance of strengthening step-level reasoning for robust performance.

item.title: Dion3: Full-Stack Orthogonal Updates [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Muon optimizer incurs a significant overhead cost due to its cubic-time Newton-Schulz orthogonalization step. When weights are sharded, communication overhead compounds this computational cost, eroding the benefits of Muon in many settings. We present Dion3, a revision of Muon that targets this overhead at every level of the stack. Our Gram Newton-Schulz algorithm reduces the FLOP cost of orthogonalization, our CuteDSL kernels accelerate it by exploiting symmetry, and our megabatching strategy reduces communication overhead. Moreover, we propose a simple change to the update rule that cuts costs even further: selecting only a fraction of the momentum matrix's rows to orthogonalize at each step. This update rule improves on Dion (another "compressed" version of Muon), in both speed and performance. Overall, Dion3 matches or improves on the loss achieved by Muon but reduces optimizer step time by up to 6x. Dion3 is available via the dion package (https://github.com/microsoft/dion) as a drop-in replacement for Muon.

item.title: FM-LLM: A frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for adapting LLMs to time series forecasting [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2608.11623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have spurred cross-modal solutions for time-series forecasting. However, existing methods rely heavily on textual prompts for modality alignment-introducing nontrivial computational overhead and failing to leverage the rich spectral dynamics inherent in time-series data.
